history.dynasty: Uncertain; local tradition says the shrine belonged to the old Vettathu Nadu; temple claimed to be ~1800 years old (legendary, not archaeologically established)
history.period: Legendary antiquity (~1800 years, unverified); razed during Tipu Sultan's campaigns (late 18th century) and rebuilt by devotees at the same spot
history.summary: The Vellamassery Garudan Kavu near Tirur is described by multiple sources as India's only temple where Garuda (the eagle-vahana of Vishnu) is worshipped as the presiding deity, shown in a flying pose. Legend says a sage performed penance here and received Vishnu's discourse on keeping people free of disease; Garuda flew by and sat by the pond (theertha), hallowing the ground. The adjacent Mahavishnu shrine is in the rare Koorma (tortoise) avatar, also said to have a white-turtle sankalpa - hence the name Vellamassery. Sources agree the temple was virtually razed to the ground during Tipu Sultan's campaigns and later rebuilt by local and distant devotees. Worship here is especially sought for recovery from disease and relief from serpent poison/venom; the temple observes the ritual Mutta Vazhipadu for Sarpa Dosham. Note: sources disagree on the presiding deity - some call Garuda the reigning deity, others say Vishnu is the main murti with Garuda as the famous upa-devata. The temple is unusual in placing no restriction of entry on anyone.

name: Vellamassery Garudan Kavu Temple
town: Triprangode (CSV town 'Malappuram' is the district, not the town; the temple is at Vellamassery near Triprangode, close to Tirur)
town_description: Triprangode is a small town in Malappuram district of Kerala, about 8-10 km from Tirur town. Tirur is a historic market town on the banks of the Bharathappuzha's old course, known for its railway junction and its association with the Malayalam literary tradition (Tunjath Ezhuthachan). The area around Triprangode is a typical Malappuram rural belt of paddy fields, coconut groves and backwater-influenced villages, served by the Tirur railway station and road links to Ponnani and Kozhikode.

travel.road: On the Tirur-Ponnani road via Triprangode; private and KSRTC buses from Tirur and Kozhikode (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: September to February (winter season); Mandalakalam (Nov 16-Dec 28) and Sundays are especially auspicious
